How Follow System works on Linux

On Linux, **Follow System** reads the XDG desktop settings portal's `org.freedesktop.appearance/color-scheme` preference and follows its live updates, including GNOME's dark-mode toggle with the standard Adwaita GTK theme. The resolved light/dark theme is applied explicitly to GTK window decorations and the webview. A portal value of `0` (no preference) resolves to light, so switching back to the desktop default cannot reuse the app's previously forced dark theme. If the portal is unavailable or returns an unsupported value, Tabularis falls back to the native window theme, then the browser media query. The default window capability grants `core:window:allow-set-theme` to allow native theme changes. macOS and Windows use native theme notifications. See the portal specification.

|🏷 Save-conflict choice|When you save in the Resume workbench and the same Resume was changed in another window, you are asked to “use the latest”, “compare the differences” or “save a copy”; **your changes never silently overwrite someone else's**|

|↪ Undo and redo|“History” in the left column: every content, typography and structure action can be undone or redone (consecutive typing collapses into one step); **each step spells out what changed** (Sections added, removed or reordered / Entries added, removed or hidden / Fields added, moved or removed / how many passages changed / typography parameters), with name, Entry count and page count on hover, and clicking a step returns you to it; a bad edit is one click away from being undone, and **⌘/Ctrl+Z and ⇧⌘/Ctrl+Z work too**. Dragging a continuous slider only updates the preview and records one step when you let go, so one undo steps back past the whole drag instead of a single tick|

|🗃 Named versions and Job variants|“Versions” at the top of the workbench: store the current content and typography as an **immutable snapshot** (create, with an optional name that is generated when left blank / freeze a marker / compare the default and the previous version Field by Field as “old → new” / restore); restoring produces **a new current version** while past versions and records already applied with stay as they are. Job variants are edited independently (create from the current Resume or from a career scenario, then “Create variant”), can **selectively sync** the content paths you tick without overwriting other Job tailoring, and can hold **their own typography** and be exported straight from the variant|

|🌐 Bilingual versions and glossary|“Bilingual versions” in the workbench: field-by-field Chinese/English comparison, translation candidates generated per Field and **accepted item by item** (only the language variant you pick is written, and the current Resume is never overwritten); a dataset-level glossary pins fixed translations (people, companies, skills and so on), and deleting an entry moves it to the trash where it can be restored. Candidates are generated in batches, so **a large Resume no longer times out mid-run**, and “Translation preview” opens a read-only preview that leaves the master document untouched and creates no dirty values|

|📦 Export shape|The export dialog starts by choosing a **delivery pack** or **individual files**: a delivery pack wraps the chosen formats into one zip (optionally archiving the originals and a hash manifest), while individual files let you multi-select formats and **export them one by one** with a progress indicator showing how many are done, and when one fails it tells you how many already succeeded. Both share the same typography result and export configuration|

|📄 Multi-format export|PDF **downloads directly** (rendered on the server); Word / HTML / Markdown / txt / JSON all export; HTML / PDF / Word and Markdown with typography are **rendered from one and the same layout result on the server** — same fields, same order — and JSON emits the new document structure (including each item's paper placement and typography); watermarks and **one-click redaction** are supported. The preview toolbar can switch to **“Exact”**, which shows exactly the PDF the export engine lays out, point for point identical to the file you download; after configuring a watermark or redaction you can **preview the real artifact** before exporting. Past the page limit it **never shrinks the font size**: it truncates at the limit and says so|

|📦 Delivery pack export|“Export delivery pack” on the Resume detail: formats and naming rules, watermark / redaction, **a preview of the real artifact configuration**, savable as an export configuration; exports a zip plus a manifest (hashed item by item) and can archive the **delivery originals** (hashes and the font / render versions used, which you can inspect and delete)|

|💾 Save location|Settings → the “Data & storage” tab → the “Save location” card: by default exports only go to the browser's download directory, and once you pick a folder with the native picker, exports from the local front end **also land a copy there**; remote or cross-site exports are refused|

|📦 Offline share pack|Packs a redacted HTML / PDF plus a read-only snapshot and a comment-return file, and can be “read-only” or “commentable”; a commentable pack supports **annotations on objects**: import the returned `annotations.json` and mark each annotation resolved or ignored, and annotations whose object changed must be re-linked (annotations never enter any applying artifact). The `resume.html` footer carries a single “Made with ResumeForge · date” line, while **exported PDF and Word files carry no logo and no footer text**|

|🚀 Automatic apply desk|Collect automatically by keyword and city (site filters are carried over wholesale and it runs in the background); confirmed Jobs queue up and drive your local browser to apply, and **only Jobs whose source is inside a recruiting site are accepted**|

|📮 Submitted & delivery receipt|On a **successful** apply record, click “I've submitted”: it adds an “applied” tracker entry (an entry already further along is never downgraded), schedules a follow-up reminder 7 days out and freezes a delivery snapshot — repeated clicks create nothing new. The “delivery receipt” in the same drawer turns that snapshot into an **inspectable record**: which Resume version went out (title + content fingerprint), to whom, export artifact and page count, which fields were filled (exact URL match against Web form fill records; a miss shows as “unknown”), how many fact-ledger doubts remain and which manual steps are still missing. Three states, **waiting on you > has doubts > ready**; “the Resume changed after delivery” is shown as information only and never changes the state|

|📝 Web form|Fills corporate application forms in a **separate dedicated browser**: type a URL to open it in a new tab and manage the URL history without clobbering pages you already have open; each page can be switched between batch and point-and-fill. It reads the whole page and checks each value before filling, or confirms a suggestion next to the input you click; fields the rules cannot recognise can be handed to the AI, which **only receives page text and field names, never your Profile values**. The browser model is shared with the apply desk but runs in its own window; fill records contain real values and stay local. **It fills, it never submits**, and passwords and verification codes are never filled automatically; **it only writes into text-like controls** — dropdowns, radio buttons, checkboxes and date pickers are left alone and honestly listed as “needs your click”; a separate **relaxed mode** can try label and context matching and click dropdown and popover options (see the next row). When filling finishes it shows the **success rate** (fields filled / readable fields on the page) and can export **redacted diagnostics that contain no Resume values**, which makes it easy to report a field it could not recognise. The address bar has no magnifier button (type a URL and press Enter); while the browser runs, “Close browser” is a circle-with-a-slash icon that shows its name on hover; and the toolbar sticks flush to the content area without covering the page header|

|🟢 Relaxed mode|The Web form's **optional exception, off by default**: once you explicitly switch it on, it tries to match unrecognised text inputs (including Custom Fields) by label and context and clicks dropdown and popover options itself (**strict option matching plus read-back verification**); in relaxed text matching, low-confidence candidates backed only by weak context are left unticked for you to confirm, and repeated experience entries are only filled when the record count and the page order can be paired. Consent and declaration checkboxes still need item-by-item confirmation; date pickers and file uploads are never touched. The Job assistant has no tool to switch it on — do it on the page or in Settings. Relaxed matching can pick wrong, so proofread after filling; a multi-value popover only acts when every value matches|

|🧠 Learnt while filling|When you hit a field **ResumeForge does not know**, **both entry points** can record it: batch mode shows one summary prompt when it finishes (**everything ticked, everything “General” by default**, and you can untick individual items), and point-and-fill puts a “Remember this” next to **every box**, so you can **record it on the spot** — **even a box it recognised but has no value for** (fill it in place without jumping to another page). Once remembered, the same field is **pre-filled automatically** next time. Each entry picks a scope: **General** (true wherever you apply) / **Scenario** (tied to an applying channel) / **This time** (recorded but never auto-filled, for one-off values such as a referral code). Source and scope can be edited or removed in the Web form profile at any time, and **values the AI recognised are labeled “AI recognised”** because it is likelier than the rules to misread a field. **Custom Fields outside the catalogue** (a supervisor's name, a lab, say) can take part in Web form filling too: normal mode accepts only a unique exact match, and relaxed mode matches by label or context and flags low confidence; when something is ambiguous or fails a safety veto it does not guess, so proofread after filling. **There is exactly one destination, the Web form profile**: Resume fields are never learnt (the code that could modify them does not exist), and passwords, verification codes and other people's details are intercepted and cannot be learnt. Everything stays local and **is never read during Resume generation**|

|🔓 Login status|The apply browser, the web-form browser and the portal cookie are **three independent logins** — one can expire without touching the others, and before this you only found out by hitting a login wall. One row each, with **Check**, **Log in again** (really opens that browser's login page; the cookie row gives you a paste box) and **Check all** (in series — two browsers at once steal focus). Opening the panel **only reads the cache**: a check really opens the browser, so it never runs on its own; when no login signal can be read it says **Unknown** rather than a false Expired; the same source is not probed twice within 60 seconds|
|🎯 Job tracker|One record per company walks from “applied → screening → assessment → interview → offer”; paste an email or a screenshot to recognise progress, and preview it before it is written|
|🗓 Calendar reminders|Set reminders for applications, interviews, referrals and so on, **color-coded by urgency** (overdue / within 24 hours / within 3 days / later), with a list and a month view|

|🔔 Follow-up sweep|With **Settings → Assistant & AI behaviour → “Task cards”** switched on (off by default), a background sweep looks at applications that are **still active and have had no update for over 7 days**: 7–21 days produces a **follow-up list card**, over 21 days a **confirm-status card** (the two never overlap); at most 5 companies per card and one card per kind per week. The card only states “N days since you applied, no status change has been recorded since”, and never claims the other side replied; you can mark each company “contacted / they replied / stop following up”, and **only the decision is recorded — the tracker status is never touched**|
|🤝 Referral management|Record the referrer, the referral code and note images, follow up by status and compute a **referral conversion rate**|

|🧭 Company research|Enter a company name (role and JD optional) and one run returns two blocks: **source cards** from web search (official site, recent news, company profile, each labeled with its site and authority) and a **web brief with numbered citations** you can expand back to the original pages; the two calls are independent, so **a failed brief never swallows the cards** (it only shows the reason); “Deep research” is off by default (multi-round search, billed per query) and the page reports how many searches ran and how long it took|

|📈 Job search analytics|Four themes — conversion and blockers, timing and pace, channels and destinations, Resume and health; **every chart is its own block with its own title and its own definition**, and trends cover the last 1 / 3 / 6 months|
|⭐ Favorites|Browse favorited Jobs and Resumes on pages, jump to a detail view or remove the favorite|

|🎤 Mock interview|Set the Job, the difficulty and the interviewer's style, then answer round by round while the interviewer comments and probes; the session closes with per-dimension scores and improvement advice; **you can keep probing below the report, or stop** (probing does not consume official rounds); material can be picked from records or imported as files (the Job side takes PDF / TXT, the Resume side takes screenshots, and a parse failure says why); **a round can be paused at any time** (the timer stops, the count is greyed out as paused, and paused time never counts toward the duration)|

|🎙 Realtime voice call|A full-screen call view: the interviewer's portrait, a breathing waveform, **the current question and your answer**, and the transcript scrolling on its own (the page itself never scrolls). Spoken answers are transcribed and sent; **the interviewer is read aloud by cloud TTS** (Bailian `qwen3-tts-flash`, default voice Cherry) synthesised sentence by sentence with the next one pre-fetched, and it **falls back to the browser voice with a visible reason** when synthesis fails — never silent. Nine parameters (voice / rate / volume / pause threshold / hold-after-filler / auto-send / barge-in sensitivity / max segment length / read-aloud) are stored on this machine, apply immediately and can be reset; with auto-send off every transcript lands as an **editable bubble** you can fix, re-say (only the latest segment) or discard, and a submitted answer can be **edited and re-asked**|

|🎯 Personalized question bank|Generates three kinds of question per Job — **basics / project deep dive / questions for HR** — with a reference answer available for any single question; real interview questions can be used to reverse-engineer edits to the Resume|

|🔎 Interview deep dive|Stress-tests the Fact ledger entry by entry, with **the criteria fixed before you ever see the question**; instead of a score it reports “verified / partly verified / unverified / contradictory”|
|🧠 Interview notes base|Captures real interview experience (company / Job / questions / retrospective) and makes it searchable, with cards that open the full text|
|📖 Knowledge base|Written material such as interview summaries, Resume tips and search strategy, with category tags and Markdown previews; the assistant can search, add and edit it|

|💬 AI Job assistant|Streaming chat that can be linked to a Job / Resume / Profile and to web search; it can look up reminders, referrals, interview notes and analytics and **only writes data when you explicitly ask**; before answering it is given the local time and weekday (late at night it suggests going to bed); its tool set covers applying-failure diagnosis, typography queries, and recording interview notes and referrals; open it from the Toutou bubble on any page; the sidebar and the floating chat keep separate histories, and the floating one only exposes web search and reasoning effort|

|🎛 Job preferences|Settings → “Assistant & AI behaviour” → “Job preferences” keeps the constraints you keep repeating (target role family, cities, salary floor, work mode, employment type, excluded companies and industries, overtime, banned words, length, tone, availability, this-conversation-only, 13 kinds in all) so a new conversation does not start from zero. **One entry = one confirmed value**; the assistant saying “noted” does not count — you pick “always” or “this conversation only” on the confirmation card. Every entry can be edited, sent to the trash, or rolled back one version, and preferences **only constrain the assistant: they never reach Resume content or the fact ledger**|

|🔓 Assistant relaxed mode|Settings → the “Assistant & AI behaviour” tab → the “Assistant relaxed mode” card: off by default; once on and **announced in advance**, the assistant may read the full Profile (including sensitive fields such as name and phone number, Web form values and past conversations), while credentials such as API keys are never sent in any mode|
|🧩 Skills|Create, import and edit skills (a prompt plus knowledge files); enable them in a conversation to shape how the assistant answers there|
|🗒 Conversation management|Rename, pin, favorite, group and archive conversations, and export them as Markdown or save them to the Material library|

|📌 Toutou clipboard|**Double-click the Toutou bubble** to open it: store snippets you paste repeatedly and copy them in one click; they only live in your local browser and are never uploaded (a single click still opens the assistant)|
|🏠 Home|Quick entries in the order you use them, across 7 destinations; the upcoming-reminders card embeds a compact month calendar|

|🔍 Global search|One box that searches Jobs, Resumes, referrals, reminders, interview notes, the Fact ledger, the Material library and Skills at once|

Identify trackers by their app/device ID and last-seen time; you can link multiple phones, and GarageStack uses the best match for each trip. See Phone GPS setup.

- **Trip log** -- Mark each trip as business, commute or private (commutes between your home and work are marked automatically), add notes, hide a GPS glitch, join two trips a fuel stop split, fix a route the car recorded badly on the map, and export a month or a year as a spreadsheet with the addresses and odometer readings a tax trip log (such as the Dutch *rittenregistratie*) asks for. - **Dutch registration (RDW)** -- For a car with a Dutch licence plate, a dashboard card with the date the APK runs out and the days left, open recalls with what can go wrong and what the dealer does about it, and whether the car is insured, from the RDW's open data. - **Home Assistant** -- Your car appears in Home Assistant automatically through MQTT discovery, sharing GarageStack's broker and MG session instead of needing a second integration. - **Progressive Web App (PWA)** -- Installable on mobile or desktop for a native app-like experience, complete with a home screen icon and push notification support. Where the browser allows it, GarageStack offers to install itself, and the offer can be turned down for good. It also opens without a connection, in an underground car park or away from home without your VPN: every page then shows what that device last loaded (the dashboard, statistics, the map with its routes, the trip log, charge history, maintenance and climate schedules) and says so and from when, the buttons that need the server (commands, editing, the log viewer) are hidden until it can be reached again, and the directions dialog still offers the coordinates and a `geo:` link for a map app with offline maps. The maps keep their streets too: the app keeps the map tiles it has shown (up to about 150 raster tiles and 400 basemap files, for a month), so the areas you looked at with a signal are there offline. It never downloads areas you have not looked at, which OpenStreetMap's tile policy forbids. The saved pages and the kept tiles are forgotten on signing out. Installing and push need HTTPS, see HTTPS.

- **Charging stations** -- Overlay nearby EV charging stations on the map, sourced from the Open Charge Map database. Station data is cached in the database for 7 days; on page load the map immediately shows all stations within 100 km of your car that are already cached. Markers show operational status; clicking a marker displays the station name, operator, address, and available connector types with power ratings. Requires a free OCM API key (`OPENCHARGEMAP_API_KEY`). Unlike fuel stations and service areas, charging station tiles are loaded on demand as you browse the map and are not pre-populated by the background Worker.

- **Place names** -- Trips are listed by where they went ("Zwolle to Deventer") instead of by date alone, and the dashboard's location card names the street the car is parked in. Sourced from OpenStreetMap via Nominatim -- no API key required, answers are cached in the database for 90 days, and the whole feature can be switched off under Settings > Map, or for the deployment with `GEOCODING__ENABLED=false`.

- **Snapped trip lines** -- A selected trip is drawn along the roads it was driven on rather than in straight lines between GPS fixes, which also gives a truer distance than the fixes alone. Matched against OpenStreetMap by Valhalla -- no API key required, snapped trips are cached in the database for 30 days, and it can be switched off in the map's filter panel or for the deployment with `MAPMATCHING__ENABLED=false`.

- **Themed vector basemap** -- Every map is drawn from OpenStreetMap vector tiles by MapLibre GL, in a dark or light style that follows the interface theme (or in full colour, if you prefer) and with labels in the interface language. Served by OpenFreeMap without an API key, point it at your own tile server if you prefer, and it falls back to raster tiles where WebGL is unavailable.

- **Single sign-on** -- Sign in through your own identity provider (Authentik, Authelia, Keycloak, Pocket ID, Google, and anything else speaking OpenID Connect), with optional auto-login and group or email based access restrictions. Every proxy in front of the API (yours, and with Compose the frontend container) is trusted by default as long as it has a private address, so visitors are told apart for the login rate limit without further setup. The catch is that anything else on your LAN is believed the same way and could claim to be a new visitor on every sign-in attempt, so in that default sign-ins are also capped per device in front of the frontend container (30 per 5 minutes; a household behind one proxy shares that). To close the gap, list each proxy in `ForwardedHeaders__TrustedProxies__0`, `__1`, ... (see CONFIGURATION.md): then only those are believed and the extra cap is off. The frontend container is one of them, and when your proxy reaches it over a Docker network, list that network as a range (`172.18.0.0/16`) rather than single addresses, which change when a container is recreated.
